questions.q: What is the essay's central advice to founders?
options: Build a polished, elegant product before opening it to any users
Hire dedicated salespeople early so engineers can focus on writing code
Wait for the market to discover your better mousetrap on its own
Do manual, unscalable work like recruiting and delighting early users
questions.explain: The essay opens with YC's advice to do things that don't scale, such as recruiting users manually.

questions.q: What did the Collison brothers do when someone agreed to try Stripe?
options: Asked for their laptop and set them up on the spot
Mailed a hand-written note to each interested founder
Sent them a link to the beta and waited for feedback
Offered a free month of service to every new company
questions.explain: The 'Collison installation' was saying 'give me your laptop' and installing Stripe immediately.

questions.q: What did Airbnb's founders do to get their marketplace started?
options: Posted listings on many classified websites to attract guests
Hired a PR firm to generate press coverage and brand awareness
Went door to door in New York, recruiting users and helping improve listings
Focused on building a polished product before reaching out to users
questions.explain: Airbnb went door to door in New York to recruit users and help existing hosts improve listings.

questions.q: Why did Ben Silbermann go to a conference of design bloggers?
options: Pinterest's earliest users were interested in design
Investors there had already offered him seed funding
He wanted to recruit designers for his early team
Airbnb's founders had recommended the conference to him
questions.explain: He noticed many early Pinterest users liked design, so he recruited at a design bloggers' conference.

questions.q: What does the author mean by 'insanely great' for an early startup?
options: The product should be flawless and feature-complete from the day of launch
The experience of being the user should be great, even if the product is buggy
The founders should work insane hours until weekly growth reaches 10 percent
The marketing should be extremely aggressive and reach millions of users quickly
questions.explain: He says it's the user's experience, not the product, that should be insanely great, made up for by attentiveness.
